The reporter prefixes each count line with U+2139 INFORMATION SOURCE and marks a failing test with U+2716 HEAVY MULTIPLICATION X; neither glyph is reproduced. The paperwork's stated reason for removing witness/release-verify-waits-for-the-registry-to-serve-the-version.json is that its members 1 to 4 stay green. delivery/evidence/m6-final-report.md:309-311: 'PR #211 (2026-09-23) added two witnesses for `scripts/release-verify.sh` and touched no `src/`, so they were never evaluated. The first full sweep found one collapsing under rule (g) and the other's members 1 to 4 staying green.' The same sentence is in delivery/tuition/T-049-a-witness-went-stale-through-a-pull-request-the-gate-skipped.md under 'Second instance (found at the M6 close)'.

MEASURED, and it refutes 'staying green' for member 1. Member 1 read from the base spec (git show 4411d74:witness/release-verify-waits-for-the-registry-to-serve-the-version.json): file 'scripts/release-verify.sh', find '    if [ $((now + POLL_SECONDS)) -gt "$deadline" ]; then
      break
    fi', replace '    if true; then
      break
    fi'. Applied by hand after confirming exactly one occurrence of the find text in the working tree; git diff scripts/release-verify.sh showed '-    if [ $((now + POLL_SECONDS)) -gt "$deadline" ]; then' / '+    if true; then', 1 file changed, 1 insertion, 1 deletion.

UNDER THE MUTATION, the three tests the spec names: 'release-verify in registry mode waits until the registry serves the version, then verifies it' -> 1 test, 0 pass, 1 fail, 0 skipped (assertion at test/license-gate.test.ts:1434, 'expected a green after the registry started serving; stderr: release-verify: NOT SERVED. The registry did not serve @tiphys/kernel@0.2.0 within 30 seconds (1 poll(s); last poll: npm cache add exited 1; last npm error: npm error code ETARGET).' ... '75 !== 0'). 'release-verify in registry mode times out with NOT SERVED and exit 75 when the registry never serves the version' -> 1 test, 0 pass, 1 fail, 0 skipped. 'release-verify in registry mode fails a served but broken version at its steps without waiting out the deadline' -> 1 test, 1 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped.

BASELINE on the same interpreter (node v26.6.0) after restoring scripts/release-verify.sh from HEAD, with git status --short showing only the untracked verdict file and git diff --stat HEAD -- scripts/release-verify.sh empty: test 1 -> 1 test, 1 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped; test 2 -> 1 test, 1 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped. So two of the three named tests are green without the mutation and red with it: member 1's dangerous state IS caught by the suite.

MECHANISM of the gate's 'member 1 red 0/2', read from src/witness/run.ts:1022: 'red: exitCode !== 0 && failed.length === tests.length'. A member counts red only when EVERY named test fails. Member 1 reddens 2 of the 3 named tests, so failed.length (2) !== tests.length (3) and the member is scored not-red; with deterministic true, src/witness/run.ts:1644-1645 ('rate.red === rate.total') then requires every repetition red, giving 'red 0/2'. The gate line is a faithful report of that predicate; it is not evidence that the mutation goes undetected.

WHY THIS IS LOW AND DOES NOT BLOCK. (i) No shipped artefact is wrong: witness/ is not in the shipped set (CLAUDE.md names schemas/, roles/, tuition/, templates/, checklists/), and the claim did not reach the shipped root tuition/ -- 'grep -rn "release-verify\|staying green\|T-049" tuition/' printed no output over the 17 entries there. (ii) NO COVERAGE CLIFF: scripts/release-verify.sh keeps FIVE witness specs at head ('ls witness/ | grep release-verify' -> release-verify-bounds-each-registry-poll.json, release-verify-polls-the-install-path.json, release-verify-refuses-contaminated-resolution-path.json, release-verify-rejects-bounds-above-a-day.json, release-verify-tarball-mode-makes-no-registry-poll.json), four of which cite the same two captures as the removed specs and which the quoted sweep evaluated without reporting them as no longer guarding. (iii) The behaviour's direct guard remains: all four tests the two removed specs named are present at head (test/license-gate.test.ts:1426, :1459, :1493, :1605) and both behaviours keep their registry rows (test/behaviors.json:991, :998). (iv) DR-0061(a) licenses the removal itself: 'Removing a rule, check, gate, test or document needs one commit with a one-line reason. No register, no inventory, no witness of the removal.'

The FIRST removal's reason is correct and is not part of this finding. witness/release-verify-served-means-the-exact-version.json at the base declares 2 members; measured, m0.file === m1.file ('scripts/release-verify.sh') and m0.find === m1.find (both '    if [ "$code" -eq 0 ] && [ "$observed" = "$VERSION" ]; then'), with only replace differing ('    if [ "$code" -eq 0 ]; then' versus '    if [ "$code" -eq 0 ] && [[ "$VERSION" == "$observed"* ]]; then'). src/witness/run.ts:1478-1487 collapses on exactly that condition ('first.file === second.file && first.find === second.find'), leaving one member against rule (g)'s two-member floor at src/witness/run.ts:1458-1467. That spec also names only one test, so the predicate above does not arise for it.
findings.analysis: Both removals are permitted by DR-0061(a), and the close-out is right that neither witness had ever been evaluated (T-049). The defect is narrower and is about the record, not the code: the recorded reason for the second removal, repeated in the owner-facing final report and in T-049, says the members 'stay green', which a reader will take to mean the mutations go undetected. For member 1 that is false. What actually happened is that the runner's red predicate requires every named test to fail, so a spec naming three tests cannot score a member red unless all three redden. The coverage was recoverable without weakening anything, since each member only needed the subset of tests it reddens. I am deliberately not raising this above low: the subject keeps five other witness specs and all four named tests, so nothing is left unguarded, and the sentence is a faithful restatement of the gate's own output in the gate's own vocabulary.
findings.concrete-fix: Two parts, neither blocking this merge. (1) Correct the wording in delivery/evidence/m6-final-report.md:309-311 and in delivery/tuition/T-049's 'Second instance' section: say that the members were scored not-red by the runner's red predicate, which requires every named test to fail (src/witness/run.ts:1022), rather than that the suite stays green under them, and note that member 1 reddens 2 of the 3 named tests when applied by hand. (2) Record as follow-up alongside the t-049-precondition item already in m6-final-report.yaml's infrastructure-left: either narrow each member's named-test list to the tests it reddens, or change the predicate to 'some named test fails' (failed.length > 0) so a multi-test spec cannot be declared non-guarding while a member is in fact caught. Until one lands, any witness naming more than one test can be retired on the same artefact.

evidence: NOT A DEFECT IN THE DIFF, recorded so the orchestrator does not read my bundle as green. The check-4 bundle came back with the suite gate RED: 'gates: suite: red: 2 finding(s): failing test: "a template copied out of an installed package validates against a schema from the same install, and removing that schema reddens" (test/license-gate.test.ts); failing test: "release-verify from a clean directory passes and records a resolved path inside the install prefix" (test/license-gate.test.ts)'. The gate's own row (/tmp/rv-close-b/suite/result.json) reads status red, units 1247, unitLabel 'tests reported'.

CAUSE: no outbound network in this review container. Re-run alone on a clean tree, 'release-verify from a clean directory passes and records a resolved path inside the install prefix' fails with 'release-verify: step install exited 1 / step import exited 1 / step bin-version exited 127 / step copy-template exited 1 / step validate-template exited 127 / release-verify: 5 failing step(s)', after 284205ms. The test (test/license-gate.test.ts:1168-1188) runs 'npm pack' and then scripts/release-verify.sh against the tarball, whose install step resolves the package's dependencies from the registry; exit 127 on the later steps is the cascade from the failed install. The sandbox here refuses outbound network commands outright, so registry reachability could not even be probed directly (CLAUDE.md warning 6 says to probe, not assume, and the probe was refused rather than answered).

NOT ATTRIBUTABLE TO THE CHANGE, established rather than assumed. The failing tests and every input they exercise are byte-identical between base and head: 'git diff --stat 4411d74...3fd70ed -- test/license-gate.test.ts scripts/ package.json package-lock.json src/ bin/ templates/ schemas/ roles/ checklists/ tuition/ plugin/' printed NO OUTPUT. The diff's 11 paths are .github/workflows/gates.yml, six files under delivery/, test/behaviors.json, test/gate-registry.test.ts and the two deleted witness/*.json specs; none is read by test/license-gate.test.ts (its witness/ reads are witness/captures/npm-pack-dry-run-json.txt, release-verify-contaminated-and-clean.txt, release-verify-registry-not-served.txt and release-verify-cache-add-not-served.txt, and 'ls witness/captures/' confirms all four survive at head). So for these two tests the base result equals the head result by construction, and I did NOT run the base separately: a base worktree would need its own npm ci, which needs the network that is blocked.

CONSISTENT WITH THE RECORD WHERE THE NETWORK EXISTS: delivery/work-history/m6-close-fix.md reports 'npm test exit 0, node v26.6.0, dist/ built: 1247 tests, 1247 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped' at e8b89f5, and m6-final-report.yaml cites PR CI run 36797496893 at 976e66f with 1246 tests, 1246 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped. My run reports the same 1247 tests, with the two network-dependent ones red.

EVERY OTHER GATE IS GREEN OR NOT-APPLICABLE, as the brief requires, and merge-preconditions is red for exactly the declared reason. Full bundle, run f12d37f14b352fbf9dcd23b3, 'gates: declared 8 applicable 6 verdict 6 green 4 red 2 not-applicable 2 error 0 vacuous 0'.
findings.analysis: This is a limitation of the review container, not a defect in the pull request, and I am reporting it rather than cleaning it up so that nobody mistakes my local bundle for the green CI run the merge actually needs. DR-0031 is the relevant rule in the other direction too: establishing green locally is the procedure, and here the local environment genuinely cannot run two of the 1247 tests because they install a packed tarball from the registry. CLAUDE.md warning 12 asks for the base's result on the same interpreter before blaming a change; I could not run the base in this container, so I settled it the other available way, by showing the two tests' inputs are byte-identical between base and head.
findings.concrete-fix: Nothing to change in the diff. Before merging, take CI green on the exact head 3fd70ed23cfeabd78532fa74033a9039ead35d1d from the GitHub pull_request run, where the registry is reachable, and quote the suite gate's own row from its summary.json rather than my local bundle; treat my check-4 lines as evidence for the other seven gates only.
